item.title: Two men charged over RAF Fairford air base incident, with one accused of assisting foreign intelligence
item.description: One of those charged, Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim, 24, has been accused of assisting a foreign intelligence service, which police believe to be Iran's.

item.title: Norwegian media sue Meta over plans to use their journalism for AI
item.description: Publishers say new terms for Facebook and Instagram business accounts could allow Meta to collect articles, images and videos from their websites without permission.

item.title: ‘Mosquito toilets’: How scientists are using mosquito poop to detect viruses
item.description: Researchers have developed a “mosquito toilet” — a tool to analyse mosquito waste for pathogens — that could be an early warning system for emerging health threats.

item.title: Neil Young sues Donald Trump's political committee for copyright infringement - again
item.description: Neil Young has filed a $10 million suit against Donald Trump's political action committee, Trump 47 Committee Inc., for using his hit song ‘Rockin’ in the Free World’ - six years after a prior settlement over the same song.

item.title: 'Unacceptable violation': Syria condemns Jordan airstrikes
item.description: A government spokesperson said Jordan had "avoided" civilian sites and that it regretted "unintended casualties," stressing that the country had "deep respect" for the Syrian state and people.

item.title: What to expect from the Fed as Warsh weighs hot inflation, oil and US midterms
item.description: The Federal Reserve is expected to keep interest rates on hold on Wednesday, six days before the US midterm elections, but with inflation at 3.7% and oil prices still elevated, investors see another hike in December as likely and will scour Chair Kevin Warsh's words for clues.

item.title: Finland's puppy livestream grips millions worldwide
item.description: A Finnish dog and her six newborn puppies have become an international online sensation. The 24/7 livestream, known as “Pentulive”, attracted 1.85 million unique viewers in its first two weeks, according to public broadcaster Yle.

item.title: Italian archaeologists discover links to tomb of Jesus underneath Jerusalem's Church of the Holy Sepulchre
item.description: Italian researchers have found a burial ground beneath Jerusalem's Church of the Holy Sepulchre, matching biblical accounts of the location of Jesus' burial.

item.title: Tashkent modernism enters the UNESCO World Heritage List
item.description: Tashkent’s modernist buildings combine new architectural ideas with local materials, patterns and climate-conscious design. Ten landmarks are now included in a UNESCO World Heritage site.

item.title: Australia warns of ‘unprecedented’ AI-powered cyberattacks. Here’s what’s driving them
item.description: The country’s cyber security agency says AI is helping criminals and state-backed hackers exploit vulnerabilities faster, as recent incidents expose risks to government systems and critical infrastructure.

item.title: Poland signs three-year defence cooperation plan with UK
item.description: UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in Warsaw the deal "sets our joint assessment of current threats and our resolve that, in the clash between freedom and tyranny, the UK and Poland will not stand aside".

item.title: Eurovision in crisis: Netherlands make U-turn and pull out of Eurovision 2027
item.description: The Netherlands has pulled out of next year's Eurovision Song Contest, with public broadcaster NPO citing "sensitivities" over Israel's participation - reversing a previous decision to participate.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz cuts 2026 profit outlook amid China market struggles
item.description: Mercedes-Benz now expects its 2026 core profit to remain flat at €5.8 billion, abandoning its earlier forecast of 15% growth, further signaling the severe structural crisis threatening Germany's automotive industry.

item.title: ‘Children first and competitors second’: Esports industry failing young players’ wellbeing, report warns
item.description: Sleep disruption, mental health pressures and online abuse are among the risks young esports players face, as a lack of common standards leaves their protection fragmented, Save the Children says.

item.title: TikTok parent company founder tops China's rich list amid AI boom
item.description: Zhang Yiming has reclaimed his position as China's richest person, with a €89.4 billion fortune driven by AI, as the country's technology sector booms while traditional industries struggle.

item.title: Dutch chip firm Besi's shares jump as Applied Materials moves to double stake
item.description: Shares in Dutch chip equipment maker Besi jumped on Tuesday after US rival Applied Materials announced plans to lift its holding to roughly 20% from 9%, tightening ties built around technology used to make AI hardware.

item.title: Football: Mbappé apologises for 'ill-judged' joke about China's Mao Zedong that led several brands to drop him
item.description: The decision came after the clip spread on social media across China, where jokes about Mao, who died in 1976, are seen as disrespectful.

item.title: To the moon and beyond: Astronauts Chris Hadfield and Victor Glover on why the 'New Space race matters
item.description: Many are called but astronauts Chris Hadfield and Victor Glover are among the few chosen to venture into outer space. In an extraordinary conversation at the Starmus VIII Festival, the pair discuss their experiences of being among the stars, science in pop culture and their hopes for humanity.

item.title: Knives, knuckledusters and a ‘Gucci robbery’: police discover chats linked to Milan riots
item.description: A 30-year-old researcher detained over the clashes in Milan has refused to answer a judge’s questions, as police investigating the unrest uncovered chats threatening officers and carried out searches across Italy.

item.title: Europe's most haunted hotels you can book a stay in this Halloween
item.description: From heartbroken lovers to airmen who have fallen to their untimely deaths, these hotels on the continent have guests with no respect for the 11am checkout time.

item.title: Why should Big Tech know what you’re working on? Scale AI accused of spying on AI trainers
item.description: The European Centre for Digital Rights, known as Noyb, is filing complaints against San Francisco-based startup Scale AI over the way its training platform Outlier tracks its 900,000 workers.

item.title: Finnish and Norwegian leaders call Putin, urge restart of peace talks
item.description: The leaders of Finland and Norway held a phone call with Vladimir Putin to restart the peace process. The overture comes as Brussels prepares for face-to-face contacts with the Russian side.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 27th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 27th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Ukraine improves jet-powered drone interception rates, but Starlink disruptions threaten progress
item.description: Ukraine made significant progress in countering Russia's jet-powered drones, with some air defence units reporting interception rates around 80%. But recent restrictions on US satellite services exposed Kyiv's reliance on US technology as it races to develop cheaper, more effective interceptors.

item.title: Funeral homes, morgues and autopsy rooms: Halloween fans seek the ‘real’ thing on paranormal tours
item.description: From former psychiatric hospitals to funeral homes, US attractions offer ghost hunts and overnight stays for Halloween fans seeking an otherworldly encounter.

item.title: Turkey: tornado kills at least four workers at Antalya construction site
item.description: At least four workers died when a tornado struck a construction site in Antalya, overturning accommodation cabins and a tower crane. Heavy rain also flooded roads in Istanbul.

item.title: From doubt to delivery: Jay-Z confirmed as headliner for 2027 Super Bowl halftime show
item.description: After days of speculation, Jay-Z, the rapper who became hip-hop's first billionaire by building a career as an executive and entrepreneur, is returning to his roots as an entertainer to perform at the Super Bowl halftime show.

item.title: Europe to remain the ‘powerhouse’ of global travel for the next decade, new report predicts
item.description: What will shape Europe’s tourism industry over the next 10 years? A new study predicts the continent’s appeal will continue to grow, with domestic and international demand set to rise across the board.

item.title: From Baku’s waterfront to the Greater Caucasus: a new winter destination within reach
item.description: Where Europe meets Asia, Azerbaijan offers crowd-free, competitively priced skiing, growing winter sports culture and diverse landscapes close to Baku.

item.title: Win or lose, Netanyahu could remain in power for months after Israeli election as Iran tensions loom
item.description: With Israel voting in its first national election since the 7 October attacks, the prospect of prolonged coalition negotiations raises questions over who will make critical security decisions amid heightened regional tensions, and whether a change of government could alter the country's course.

item.title: Ukraine: firefighters battle flames and rescue dog from Kyiv ruins
item.description: A Russian missile and drone attack on Kyiv killed one person and injured 15. Emergency workers rescued a dog from the rubble, while strikes damaged university buildings and a major bridge.

item.title: AI chip boom tripled South Korea's economic growth in the third quarter
item.description: South Korea's economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter. However, analysts warned that its heavy reliance on the chip industry leaves the country vulnerable to a slowdown in global AI spending.

item.title: Macklemore begins Free Palestine tour in Europe with call for unity in Dublin
item.description: "I am proud to stand here on stage in solidarity with the Palestinian people. We will continue to fight for collective liberation until our last breath," Macklemore said on stage in Dublin last night.

item.title: Israelis head to polls in first general election since 7 October attacks with no clear favourite
item.description: With no party expected to win an outright majority, weeks of coalition talks could follow a vote being closely watched in European capitals.

item.title: Trump calls Norway a ‘shithouse country’ over Nobel Peace Prize snub
item.description: US President Donald Trump has launched a fresh verbal attack on Norway, branding the Nordic nation a “shithouse country”.

item.title: Rogue AI, cyberattacks and weapons: the risks Anthropic is warning investors about ahead of its IPO
item.description: The AI company’s IPO paperwork warns of potential harms from increasingly autonomous systems, alongside financial and regulatory challenges.

item.title: Star Trek actor Walter Koenig, who played Pavel Chekov, dies aged 90
item.description: Koenig's death leaves William Shatner, who played Capt. James T. Kirk, and George Takei, who played Hikaru Sulu, as the only surviving members of the original series' main cast.

item.title: Merz courts Asian investors as he insists Europe remains a safe bet
item.description: The German chancellor's upbeat pitch comes at a time of mounting pressure in Berlin, where a ministerial resignation and rising far-right support have left the chancellor’s coalition on shaky ground.

item.title: Israel: October 7 families remember victims as voters head to polls
item.description: In Tel Aviv, families affected by the 7 October 2023 attacks observed a moment of silence as polling stations were opening across Israel for the general election.

item.title: EU Inc: Why the Commission's perfect startup plan might be falling apart
item.description: EU Inc, the Commission’s promise to strengthen the EU’s startup market and keep startups from moving abroad, is facing roadblocks that make its adoption by 2026 difficult. Will the 28th regime survive?

item.title: European natural gas prices soar: What it means for your winter bills
item.description: Gas prices have tripled in 2026 and EU storage is at a record low. Analysts explain what it means for winter bills and how long it could last.

item.title: A pivotal election in Israel, and Netanyahu’s next test
item.description: Good morning. It’s Tuesday, and this is what’s on today’s docket: Election fever spreads to Israel, Zelenskyy bemoans a lack of American Patriot missiles, and the European continent is only getting hotter, according to the EU climate chief. I’m Angela Skujins. Let’s dive in.

item.title: Harry Kane is first Bundesliga player since Matthias Sammer to win Ballon d'Or
item.description: The Bayern Munich striker's award ends a decades-long wait for a Bundesliga player or Englishman to receive the prestigious trophy.

item.title: Scientists uncover new clues to the actual night sky behind Van Gogh’s The Starry Night
item.description: Researchers led by South Korean scientist Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim argue that Vincent van Gogh's painting may show the Taurus constellation rather than Aries, challenging the accepted timeline of the impressionist masterpiece.

item.title: Europe Today: Israel votes on Netanyahu's future as Orbán is floated for UN chief
item.description: Israelis vote today in their first election since 7 October, with Benjamin Netanyahu's future on the line. Washington is reportedly floating Viktor Orbán for UN secretary-general. And we interview EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra to ask what Lula's re-election means for Europe.

item.title: London’s most famous shopping street is now pedestrianised
item.description: Ahead of the holiday season, cars, buses and bikes are banned from nearly a kilometre of Oxford Street.

item.title: Deadly parasite: How fox tapeworm warns of pandemic X
item.description: The WHO has developed an early warning system to spot looming pandemics. Tropical medicine expert Dr Carsten Köhler from Tübingen explains the background to Euronews.

item.title: Europe must prepare for a 3°C warmer world, EU climate chief warns
item.description: As Brussels warns that Europe must prepare for increasingly extreme weather, new EU rules will require governments to clarify who is responsible for climate preparedness – but no new funding is being offered to help households adapt.

item.title: Blood test could reveal prostate cancer risk more than a decade before diagnosis
item.description: Proteins present in men’s blood could give clues to prostate cancer risk years before diagnosis.

item.title: Dog scared of fireworks? Switzerland could bring in a nationwide ban if public votes yes
item.description: Fireworks were banned in the Netherlands earlier this year on safety and environmental grounds.
